title: Outbound email delivery via SMTP transit peers
description:
Users who compose an article via JMAP Email/set or NNTP POST may want that article delivered as email to internet recipients (e.g. mailing lists, direct email). Add an outbound SMTP delivery path: a configured list of authenticated SMTP transit peers. No MX lookup, no direct-to-MX delivery — this is relay-only. Each peer is an SMTP relay with credentials (SASL PLAIN/LOGIN over TLS or mTLS). The peer list is operator-configured and static; no auto-discovery.

Peer selection must be health-aware: peers go up and down, so the system must not lock onto whichever peer happened to succeed last. Required behavior:
- Track per-peer up/down state with a last-success and last-failure timestamp
- On each delivery attempt, prefer peers marked up; try down peers after a backoff window
- Round-robin or weighted shuffle across currently-up peers so load distributes
- On delivery failure, mark the peer down and immediately retry with the next available peer
- On delivery success, mark the peer up but continue rotating — do not make it sticky
- Expose per-peer health in admin metrics (attempts, successes, failures, last-seen-up)
